tytul: Fish garum with koji: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for fish garum, a fermented sauce made from mackerel or sardines with koji, in the style of ancient Roman garum.

ostrzezenia.tekst: A study of botulism in Alaska found that toxin type E causes more than 85% of cases there, because many traditional foods, such as salmon heads, fish eggs, seal meat and whale blubber, are fermented in conditions that may favor Clostridium botulinum type E. Botulism from toxin type E is linked only to eating aquatic animals.
The BC Centre for Disease Control reports that botulism outbreaks have been linked to ungutted fish used to make fesikh, a fermented salted fish.

akapity: The Codex standard for fish sauce applies to fish sauce made by fermenting a mixture of fish and salt.
The Codex standard also sets a limit for histamine in fish sauce.
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for fish garum, with or without koji, from a checked source.
